businessModel: Free browser; services via Astian Account (MidoriVPN, Midori Sync, Astian Cloud, Marketplace). Revenue model details unverified
paidNote: MidoriVPN is a separate service; pricing unverified
updateCadence: Irregular; over two months with no desktop update before 11.9.x, per Astian blog
summary: The former lightweight WebKitGTK Midori, now a Firefox-based browser run by Astian with an optional Astian Account for E2EE Midori Sync (alpha) and MidoriVPN. Midori 12 is in development.
bestFor: Users wanting a Firefox-based browser with bundled sync and VPN options
Android users wanting an alternative Gecko-style browser
notFor: People wanting a long-established independent browser
Anyone needing verified security patch timelines

pros.title: Gecko base
pros.detail: Switched to tracking latest Firefox from 11.6.1 (March 2026) instead of ESR.

pros.title: Own sync
pros.detail: Midori Sync is E2EE but still in open alpha.

pros.title: Astian Account
pros.detail: Optional single account for Sync, MidoriVPN and Astian Cloud.

pros.title: Cross-platform
pros.detail: Linux, Windows, macOS (since 11.5.2 in 2025) and Android.

cons.title: Update gaps
cons.detail: Astian blog noted over two months without a desktop update.

cons.title: Alpha services
cons.detail: Midori Sync is open alpha and VPN is not fully integrated.

cons.title: Opaque details
cons.detail: Patch lag, telemetry and company jurisdiction are not clearly documented.

cons.title: Confusing lineage
cons.detail: Old WebKitGTK Midori and Android versions use a different version line.

faq.q: What engine does Midori use now?
faq.a: Gecko; it moved from WebKitGTK to a Firefox base after merging with Astian in 2019.

openSource: LGPL-2.1 per Wikipedia; Astian service code not fully open
longevity: Long history but irregular updates; Midori 12 pending
